title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
why: Shows MiniWoB++ web-agent policies encode harness preferences; ceiling vs mismatch predicts when harness changes help after retraining.
mechanism: Environment/harness theory for GUI/web agents: under KL-regularized control, trained policies carry training-harness action preferences; deployed return = harness ceiling − policy mismatch; fixed-model harness comparisons mix both terms. Empirics on MiniWoB++ (obs-field order swap 85.0%→19.2%) and Terminal-Bench Lite coding harnesses
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): MiniWoB++ harness-order swap drops success 85.0%→19.2% with optimal decisions unchanged; every ceiling-raising harness rejected by fixed-model comparison outperforms after retraining; ceiling−mismatch predicts gains; Terminal-Bench Lite ranking recovered by ceiling−mismatch with stronger model as optimum stand-in — not independently verified.

title: Odysseys2: A Web Agent Benchmark Based on Real User Requests
why: 100 live-web long-horizon tasks with stricter file-aware rubrics; successor to Odysseys for web-agent evaluation.
mechanism: Evaluation for web agents: Odysseys successor with 100 live-web long-horizon tasks (8–12 pass/fail rubric checks each), stricter Odysseys2 judge that also reads delivered files, harness comparison (BrowserCode/Pi/Python library), and public tasks+scores release
